body.x: At CES 2026, the world’s largest IT and electronics exhibition, NEWJAK Co. Ltd. (CEO Haehyun Jung) made its strategic direction unmistakably clear. Long perceived as an entertainment technology company, NEWJAK officially declared its transition into an XR platform company, positioning XR as a core infrastructure connecting defense, education, and public sectors.

The official theme of CES 2026, “Innovators Show Up,” signals a shift in expectations. Innovators are no longer expected to hide behind technology, but to step forward and take responsibility for its direction and impact. CEO Jung emphasized that “innovation is not about technology itself, but about attitude,” referencing AMD CEO Lisa Su’s CES keynote statement that AMD would take responsibility for the pace of AI advancement. NEWJAK, he explained, stood at CES with the same mindset.

body.cap: Visitors experience NEWJAK’s XR interactive sports content ‘SPORTRACK’ at the CES 2026 exhibition. The platform combines real-world movement with XR graphics, without requiring HMDs.| Photo – AVING News

body.x: “Exhibition-Only XR Is Over”… From Military Training Centers to Public Sector Deployment

According to Jung, many still view NEWJAK through the lens of entertech, but that perception no longer reflects reality. “We are not just creating XR content,” he said. “We are building an XR platform capable of operating entire service structures across industries.”

A representative example is defense. NEWJAK recently deployed its XR system at the Nonsan Army Training Center’s Mental Strength Education Facility, introducing XR-based content not for shooting or tactical drills, but for psychological and values-based training. The project is regarded as one of the earliest cases where XR has been practically adopted within a public defense education environment. Jung noted, “Immersion and comprehension are critical in military education as well. XR can fundamentally change how training is delivered.”

Implementation has also begun in education. NEWJAK completed delivery of an AI-powered XR learning playground at an elementary school in Goyang, where students engage in content that integrates physical activity with learning. Discussions are also underway with the Hanam Public Health Center regarding XR applications in public services, signaling expansion beyond defense and education.

body.cap: A visitor interacts with immersive visuals projected across the floor and walls inside NEWJAK’s six-sided XR space. The experience requires no wearable devices, relying solely on physical movement.| Photo – AVING News
Overseas visitors listen to explanations of NEWJAK’s XR platform and real-world use cases at the company’s booth within the Jeonnam Technopark joint pavilion at CES 2026.| Photo – AVING News

body.x: “Drop a Pin on Google Maps, Done in 10 Minutes”… A Field-Ready XR Platform

The technological strength of NEWJAK’s XR platform lies in speed and immediacy. According to Jung, by simply selecting coordinates on Google Maps, real-world distances and environments can be converted into XR simulations in under 10 minutes. This eliminates the need for physical mockups or lengthy environment preparation, enabling instant indoor simulations.

Such capability proves critical in time-sensitive fields such as defense and disaster response. “When situations are urgent, traditional preparation-heavy methods fall short,” Jung said. “XR platforms can provide immediate alternatives.”

This platform-oriented approach aligns closely with NEWJAK’s recognition at the CES 2026 Innovation Awards. The company drew attention with SPORTRACK, an XR interactive sports platform that allows multiple participants to engage simultaneously without head-mounted displays. Designed as a board-game-style system incorporating 16 XR physical education maps aligned with Korea’s 2023 revised national curriculum, the platform enables full physical education classes to take place even in a standard 6m × 6m classroom.

Jung concluded, “We do not see XR as a single industry. Starting from entertainment, moving through defense, education, and public services, we envision XR becoming a core interface across industries.” As CES 2026 shifts the central question from “What can be built?” to “Who will take responsibility?”, NEWJAK is stepping forward with its XR platform as a direct answer.
